description.main: A novel in which a billionaire's brain is scanned after his death and the data builds a virtual world of its own.
description.extended:
Fall; or, Dodge in Hell is a novel about what follows when a dead man's mind is kept as data and starts building a world.

Richard "Dodge" Forthrast, a billionaire, is declared brain-dead. Under his will his body is cryonically preserved and his brain is destructively scanned, with the connectome saved digitally. Years later his grandniece Sophia runs the connectome as a senior-thesis experiment, and it builds a virtual world that comes to resemble a medieval fantasy setting. The struggle over that world pits Dodge against El, a dying billionaire who takes control of it and sets up a religion around himself. William Morrow published the hardcover on June 4, 2019.

Dodge first appeared in Reamde (2011), the novel that precedes this one. Both books share a fictional universe with Cryptonomicon and The Baroque Cycle, which ties the novel back to the earlier strand of Stephenson's fiction.
